About Linkfire and where we're heading

Linkfire is the marketing platform the music industry uses to connect fans with the music they love. Trusted by major labels including Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, Sony Music Entertainment and BMG, as well as thousands of independent artists, labels, and podcasters, our smart links, bio links, and landing pages power music discovery and engagement every day.

We recently launched Artist Workspaces, giving every artist their own home on Linkfire and the foundation for a new generation of fan intelligence features. Our next chapter is about helping artists and their teams really know their fans: who they are, what they care about and how to reach them again. That means selling more tickets and more merch, and building fan relationships that last well beyond release week.

We have a packed roadmap heading into 2027, and it's vital that our customers know about the features we're shipping and see the value in them. That's where you come in.

The role

We're back in growth mode and rebuilding marketing, starting with this role. For now you'll operate as our solo in-house marketer, owning product marketing end to end. You'll report to the Director of Product and work closely with our product managers and commercial team.

The first job is clear: get our existing customers using what we've built, and turn their results into stories that help us sell to others.

You'll start with our owned channels (email, in-app, our website and socials) and our artist and label relations managers. You'll also have budget to get in front of customers, through industry events, visits to key clients and getting our message out more widely. If webinars or other new channels make sense, you can lead building them.

This isn't a performance marketing role. We expect to add performance and acquisition marketing when the time is right, as a dedicated function with its own resources, not an extra job on top of this one.

As marketing grows, there's a path to building and leading a team covering brand and identity, website, socials, and the onboarding journeys that convert new customers and keep existing ones.

What you will do

• Own the go-to-market for every feature and product launch: the narrative, who hears what and when, and the comms, assets and sends.

• Drive adoption and measure it, so we know which campaigns move usage and which don't.

• Identify customers getting value from the product, and turn their stories into case studies, testimonials, and content snippets our commercial team can use in sales conversations.

• Run our owned channels, from email and in-app to the website and socials, and own the tooling behind them.

• Represent Linkfire at industry events and in meetings with key customers.

What we are looking for

You might be a product marketer, a customer or lifecycle marketer, or a generalist who has run marketing on your own. The title matters less to us than what you've done.

• Several years in B2B or SaaS marketing, with a track record of launching features to existing customers and getting them used.

• Positioning instincts. You can work out who a feature is for, what problem it solves and why it matters, then build the launch around that.

• Hands-on experience with customer messaging tools such as Intercom, including segmentation and automation.

• Clear, persuasive writing in English. You can turn a technical feature into something a busy label marketer or artist manager will actually read.

• An eye for design and comfort creating content yourself. You’ll produce visuals and short videos for launches, working with our designer on the bigger pieces.

• Comfort with data. You set up tracking, read the results and change what you do because of them.

• An eye for a good customer story, and the persistence to get it signed off and published.

• You already use AI in your daily work and have opinions about where it helps and where it gets in the way.

Nice to have

• Knowledge of the music industry, or another creator or entertainment market.

• An interest in how fan and customer data gets captured and used, whether from working with CRM or CDP tools or just being curious about it.

• Experience working asynchronously in a distributed team.

Location

We’d love you to be based in Copenhagen or elsewhere in Denmark. We’re a distributed company and plenty of our colleagues are fully remote, but we have a cosy office on Rentemestervej where many of us visit a couple of days a week. This helps us stay in sync and we’d like it if you can join us.

English is our working language, and all our customer comms are in English too, so you don’t need to speak Danish.

How to apply

Along with your CV, tell us about a feature launch you ran: what you did, and what happened to adoption afterwards. A couple of paragraphs is plenty.

Why join Linkfire

• Real ownership from day one. How we launch and talk to customers is yours to shape.

• Be part of what's next. We're changing what Linkfire offers, and you'll help tell that story.

• A product people already use. Millions of fans interact with our customers' landing pages every day, so there's real usage to build on.

• Flexible, distributed team. Colleagues across several countries, a Copenhagen office for those who want to be together, and working hours that fit around your life.

• Benefits. Six weeks’ paid holiday and a 4% company pension contribution.

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

jobs.description:
Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant, or outsourcing company.

Join a team of fintech heroes! 🚀

Performativ is changing the way investment advisors and financial institutions operate. We are building a modern platform for portfolio management, reporting, compliance, trading, and client engagement—replacing fragmented systems, manual workflows, and technology built for another era.

Our customers include wealth managers, asset managers, family offices, and financial institutions across Europe and beyond. We are on an ambitious scaling journey, supported by leading global venture capital investors, and are working to become the platform on which modern wealth management runs.

You can read more about our product at performativ.com.

As our new Senior Software Engineer — Wealth Management Systems 📈

You will help the team solve some of the hardest product and data problems across Performativ’s investment platform.

You will work where financial workflows, product decisions, and technical systems meet: portfolio data, reporting, fees, reconciliation, instruments, transactions, cash, performance, and trading. Your contribution will be turning that complexity into coherent solutions that work across customers rather than becoming a collection of one-off customisations.

This is not a narrowly scoped position. We work as one team, and you should be willing to tackle any important problem within our area.

• 
You will apply deep experience from wealth management, asset management, private banking, portfolio management, investment operations, trading, custody, or related financial infrastructure to develop sound product and system designs.

• 
You will investigate problems that cross financial data, calculations, APIs, integrations, operational processes, and production systems—determining their root causes and delivering reliable solutions that others can understand and extend.

• 
You will bring product thinking to ambiguous requirements, working closely with users and customer-facing colleagues to distinguish reusable platform needs from customer-specific preferences.

• 
You will use AI agents to produce much of the implementation. We expect you to design the solution, direct agents effectively, challenge their assumptions, review their output, and establish the tests and evidence needed for safe production deployment.

• 
You will lead when your knowledge makes you the right person to lead, follow through on what you take on, contribute to the work of others, and help teammates succeed.

Experience with performance calculations, valuations, fees, reporting, reconciliation, corporate actions, or portfolio-management systems would be particularly valuable.

We value your passion 🔥

At Performativ, we are builders first. We have ambitious goals and value the time, judgment, and effort people put into their work. You will be trusted to make your mark and help shape how we solve difficult problems.

We do not divide the platform into personal territories. People develop deeper context in different areas, but we solve problems as a team. Autonomy works only when paired with initiative, collaboration, sound judgment, and follow-through.

AI increases our delivery speed, but it does not reduce our engineering standard or our accountability for the result. You must be technically strong enough to recognise weak abstractions, incorrect assumptions, missing edge cases, security problems, and unsafe production behaviour.

This role is based in Copenhagen. We work together primarily from our city-centre office, with flexibility to work from home when it makes sense. You should already be based in Copenhagen or be ready to relocate.

What we can offer you 🌱

• 
Trust and meaningful responsibility from your first day, with the opportunity to influence both our platform and how we build it.

• 
Difficult and consequential problems involving financial data, product design, reliability, security, and real operational workflows.

• 
The opportunity to define an AI-native approach to developing complex financial software and see your work reach customers quickly.

• 
An ambitious, collaborative team with experience from leading technology companies, consultancies, and financial institutions.

• 
Strong opportunities for professional development as Performativ grows into a European market leader.

Architect, build, and scale AI systems that hold up in production

Take ownership of how AI is architected, built, and scaled across our products. You will design the agentic systems at the core of our pension and advisory platforms, with a focus on reliable and responsible AI.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to help lead our newly established AI team, working on our Life product for pension companies. The team is focused on the practical and responsible use of AI and is still in its early stages, so as a senior member you will play a defining role in setting the technical foundation, design patterns, and ways of working that the rest of the team builds on.

You will work closely with the AI Team Lead and Chief Architect, who own the overall architecture, helping shape the design within that direction. You will also be part of an agile team with a flat structure, where collaboration, curiosity, and continuous learning are central to the culture.

This role is primarily about designing and building agentic and LLM systems end to end, with a meaningful share of your time spent owning how we evaluate them and prove they hold up. It suits someone with 5+ years of relevant experience who wants to move beyond implementation into designing AI systems, and who enjoys raising the bar for the engineers around them.

Why this matters

This is core infrastructure, not edge tooling. Our Life product runs policy and capital administration for some of Europe’s largest pension providers, including PensionDanmark and APG, and is on track to support more than 8 million members and over €800bn in retirement assets.

The AI you design must meet that bar: fast and innovative, but also accurate, secure, and reliable enough for systems that people depend on for their financial security in retirement. Building it well and being able to prove it works, are two sides of the same job.

What you’ll do

As a senior member of the AI team, you will help shape how we build with Large Language Models and agentic systems across our products, contributing to high‑level design decisions, turning ambiguous business problems into robust system designs, and ensuring high‑quality coding standards and design. You will be hands‑on, with a real say in the architecture, standards, and technical judgement that guide the team.

In practice, you will:

Help shape the technical direction

• Contribute to the AI tech stack across our products: help define the high‑level system design, reference architectures, and design patterns the team builds on.

• Help shape AI strategy: identify where AI can create genuine value, frame the trade‑offs, and feed into a coherent, prioritised technical roadmap that fits our wider platform.

• Inform major architectural decisions: model and framework selection, build‑versus‑buy, and how AI components fit into our existing Java platform, integrate with surrounding systems, scale, and stay maintainable over time.

• Reason about trade‑offs in the open: weigh latency, cost, accuracy, security, and reliability, and explain and defend those choices to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Architect and build (hands‑on)

• Design LLM systems end to end: from retrieval, agent orchestration, and data pipelines through to deployment and monitoring.

• Design and build agentic systems: single‑ and multi‑agent, covering orchestration, tool use, action groups, knowledge‑base integrations, and patterns such as routing, delegation, parallelisation, and result aggregation for complex, reliable production workflows.

• Engineer RAG pipelines that connect agents to internal structured and unstructured data.

• Drive quality through design: prompt strategy, system prompts, and memory systems that produce hallucination‑resistant outputs with strong relevance and faithfulness.

• Make cost‑aware architectural choices: balancing latency, cost, and quality across model selection and orchestration patterns so what we ship is sustainable at scale.

• Set the standards for prompt strategy, RAG, orchestration, and cost management that the wider team adopts.

Evaluate and prove

• Build evaluation frameworks: eval sets, golden datasets, and LLM‑as‑judge pipelines, with offline regression suites wired into CI and online evaluation on production traces.

• Evaluate the whole agent, not just the answer: task success, trajectory and tool‑use correctness, and RAG faithfulness and grounding, so you know whether failures come from retrieval, reasoning, or generation.

• Measure what gates shipping: relevance, faithfulness, latency, cost, and reliability across repeated runs, turned into quality gates the team ships against.

Collaborate and grow the team

• Collaborate and mentor: work with the AI Team Lead, Chief Architect, senior developers, and product teams to translate business needs into working, well‑tested solutions, and support more junior engineers as the team grows.

What we’re looking for

You bring a strong technical foundation, hands‑on depth with modern AI tooling, and the judgement to design systems that hold up in the real world. You don’t need deep expertise in every area below, but we do expect real depth in agentic systems and AI architecture, backed by a solid grasp of how to evaluate what you build.

Required

• A master’s degree in computer science or a similar field, preferably with an AI focus.

• 5+ years building software, with significant hands‑on work applying Large Language Models.

• Strong proficiency in a statically typed, object‑oriented language, Java or C# (we build in Java). Python is welcome for demos, evaluation tooling, and experiments, but it is not our production language.

• Deep experience designing, building, and operating agent‑based systems, with hands‑on use of one or more orchestration frameworks (e.g. LangChain/LangGraph, Microsoft Agents, Claude Agent SDK, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel).

• A track record of designing and building AI systems, including how the components fit together, scale, and are maintained over time.

• Solid, practical experience with prompt strategy, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and the cost considerations of LLM usage and model selection.

• Working knowledge of LLM and agent evaluation: eval sets, LLM‑as‑judge, and the metrics that distinguish a good system from a confident‑but‑wrong one (faithfulness, relevance, task success, latency, and cost).

• Experience designing AI or backend systems that fit into a larger production platform, collaborating with senior engineers and architects to align on a shared technical direction.

• Strong communication skills to explain and defend architectural trade‑offs to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Nice to have

• Experience building automated evaluation pipelines or CI gates for AI systems.

• Familiarity with observability and tracing tooling for LLM applications (e.g. LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Braintrust).

• Familiarity with LLM evaluation, automation, and red teaming.

• Broader machine learning experience.

• Hands‑on experience building and integrating MCP servers.

• Experience working in regulated or high‑reliability domains such as finance, insurance, or healthcare.

Who you are

You are a confident, hands‑on engineer who takes ownership of complex and sometimes undefined problems, and who is just as comfortable designing a system as proving it holds up. You think in systems, balance pragmatism with quality, and care about building things that work in production rather than just in a demo. You lift the people around you, stay open to feedback, and bring strong technical judgement of your own. You are curious, persistent, and result‑oriented.

jobs.occupation: Program Manager - HR Shared Services Center, Global HR
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced and driven Program Manager to lead the establishment of HR Shared Services Center (SSC), a key pillar in our HR transformation journey, driving the design, planning, and implementation of this strategic initiative.

In this role, you will establish a program organization and lead multiple workstreams and coordinate timelines, resources, budgets, stakeholders and risks to ensure the successful implementation of our HR Shared Services Center. You know which priorities to recommend, what to communicate to the HR organization and when to involve other corporate functions if necessary. Furthermore, you will bring together people, processes, technology and organisational change to establish an efficient, scalable and high-quality HR service delivery model.

**Welcome to Global HR

**You will join Demant's Global HR organization and work closely with HR Core Deliveries, business units, Shared Services C operations teams and stakeholders across the global organization.

Our approximately 400 HR professionals work globally to attract, develop and empower the people who drive Demant's continued success. As a global leader in hearing healthcare and hearing aid technology, Demant is on an ambitious transformation journey. In this role, you will help shape how HR services are delivered and experienced across the organization.

**Lead the HR Shared Services Center Transition

**As Program Manager for HR SSC, you will manage the day-to-day implementation of the SSC transition, coordinating multiple workstreams and ensuring alignment throughout the implementation. Working closely with senior leadership, HR Core Deliveries, business units, SSC operations and project leads, you will maintain momentum, manage risks and dependencies, and ensure clear communication and decision-making. You will also help ensure business continuity and successful adoption of the new HR service delivery model.

In this role, you will:

• Lead program delivery, including plans, milestones, budgets, KPIs, governance and coordination of multiple workstreams.

• Be responsible for the business case

• Track project progress against established milestones, KPIs and business case

• Drive stakeholder alignment and communication, facilitating collaboration across senior leadership, HR, business units and SSC operations.

• Manage resources, risks and dependencies, ensuring appropriate allocation of capacity and timely escalation and resolution of issues.

• Oversee transition and change activities, supporting adoption and maintaining business continuity throughout implementation.

• Ensure effective reporting and project governance, including dashboards, steering committee materials, decisions, actions and lessons learned.

• Ensure quality and compliance, including appropriate acceptance criteria and consideration of country-specific legal and regulatory requirements.

**What You Bring

**You hold a bachelor's or master’s degree in business administration, Human Resources, Project Management, Organizational Development or a related field.

You have significant project management/program management experience, including large-scale transformation or Shared Services Center establishment and transition initiatives. You have successfully managed complex, multi-workstream projects involving substantial budgets and diverse stakeholders, preferably within HR operations or HR transformation.

You have great knowledge of project management methodologies and tools. PMP certification or equivalent is an advantage, as is experience with platforms such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Asana or similar.

Experience with HR systems and processes is important, with knowledge of SAP SuccessFactors, ServiceNow or similar solutions considered an advantage. You are also highly proficient in Microsoft Office and comfortable working with project dashboards, reporting and data. As a colleague, you are structured, collaborative and solution oriented. You create clarity and momentum in complex environments and can lead cross-functional teams without direct authority. You communicate assertively with both project teams and senior executives and are comfortable working across cultures and geographies.

Furthermore, you are analytical and pragmatic, with good problem-solving and stakeholder management skills. You combine project management discipline with business acumen and an understanding of HR operations and organisational dynamics.

Finally, you have a good compliance mindset and understand the importance of balancing country-specific requirements with global standards and objectives.

**Come and join us

**This is an opportunity to take a central role in a significant HR transformation and help shape the future delivery of HR services across Demant.

You will work with experienced colleagues and senior stakeholders across the global organization and have the opportunity to make a tangible impact on how HR services are delivered, scaled and continuously improved.

If you enjoy complex transformations, international collaboration and turning ambitious plans into successful execution, we would like to hear from you.

**Come and join us

**Send your CV before application deadline November 2.

For inquiries regarding the application process, please use the online application form.

If you would like to know more about the position, you are welcome to contact Vice President, Global HR Core Deliveries, Maj Øhle Storri, via email mjsr_@demant.com

_We are curious to meet you.

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

The Senior Director, Transformation Office Portfolio Lead is a key role within Genmab’s Transformation Office (TO). The Senior Director will be the central orchestrator for operational and strategic initiatives, including initiative intake, prioritization, governance, reporting, and portfolio performance management. You will ensure that Genmab's most strategic initiatives are aligned with organizational priorities and deliver measurable business value. The initial focus of the Transformation Office is on R&D and Tech Ops (approximately 2,000 FTE), with potential for future scope expansion across the enterprise (⁓3,000 FTE).

The Transformation Office Portfolio Lead partners closely with senior business leaders, initiative sponsors, project managers, finance business partners and functional teams to drive rigorous initiative portfolio management, accelerate execution, and provide transparency on progress, risks, dependencies, and value realization.

As a key driver of the Transformation Office, the Senior Director will lead initiative portfolio management processes, develop recommendations on initiative prioritization, sequencing, and TO resource allocation, and ensure decisions are translated into action to maximize organizational impact.

The Senior Director, Transformation Office Portfolio Lead will report directly to Head of the Transformation Office (currently the SVP, Global Head of PPM & R&D Operations). The position can be located in Plainsboro, NJ, Utrecht, NL or Copenhagen, DK.

Responsibilities

·        Own portfolio management for cross-functional transformation initiatives that support Genmab’s financial commitments and strategic objectives

·        Support the Transformation Office’s goals and objectives, aligned with the company’s overarching strategy and 2030 Vision

·        Lead initiative intake screening, categorization, and prioritization processes, ensuring consistent application of prioritization criteria and governance framework

·        Support, challenges and monitors projects, initiatives, and analyses focused on company transformation and productivity gains to inform strategic capital allocation and resourcing decisions

·        Collaborate closely with Finance on Genmab’s long-range financial plan and annual budget cycle

·        Drive the organization’s ongoing mindset shift toward productivity and prioritization

·        Drive execution of initiatives from initiation through closure, ensuring clear ownership, milestones, and follow-through

·        Track, report, and communicate TO initiatives to major stakeholders at all governance levels, including progress, risks, dependencies, and value realization

·        Define, establish, and continuously monitor Transformation Office portfolio KPIs and success measures, ensuring transparent reporting of initiative performance, value realization, and overall portfolio health

·        Lead the coordination and preparation of TO meetings and serve as meeting moderator

·        Report on industry trends and peer company developments, translate their impact on Genmab, and improve overall strategic decision-making quality

·        Work cross-functionally with R&D, Tech Ops, Commercialization, Finance, Human Resources, DD&AI, and other teams to drive alignment and execution

Qualifications and Requirements

Qualifications

·        A minimum of 15 years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree in life sciences, business administration, economics or finance required is required; advanced degree (Master's, PhD) preferred.

• Prior management consulting with direct biotech/pharma case experience advising clients on company transformations required

• Prior biotech/pharma operating experience in a Transformation Office capacity and/or program and project management with a Finance background also highly valued

Requirements

• Passionate about life sciences and Genmab’s purpose and mission

• Demonstrated knowledge and expertise to drive company transformations and productivity initiatives

·        Experience preparing executive-level materials and presenting recommendations to senior leadership and governance bodies

·        Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills across the different levels within the organization

·        Highly organized, attentive to detail, and results-driven, with a strong affinity for financial analysis, business performance metrics, and value realization

·        Highly self-motivated, with the ability to take ownership, drive activities independently, and manage multiple priorities

·        Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders, drive alignment, and achieve outcomes across cross-functional teams without direct authority

·        Structured problem-solving skills

DKK962.880,00---1.444.320,00

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Join Copenhagen Energy Trading as our next Quantitative Researcher - Algorithmic Trading (Short-term Power Markets)

Copenhagen Energy Trading (CET) shapes the future of the energy transition by combining deep market expertise with technical excellence in data, quantitative research and engineering to drive, automate and optimise our trading operations.

We’re a small, elite team based in central Copenhagen specializing in power trading and asset management across Europe and North America. Technology is core to how we operate, powered by exceptional talent and one of Europe’s most advanced automated and analytical trading environments for power markets. But we're not done. We want to push automation and advanced analytics even further, and to do that we need more exceptional people.

The Opportunity

That’s where you come in. We’re looking for an outstanding Quantitative Researcher with a proven track record of building real-time algorithmic trading strategies that operate with high reliability in regulated industries. You'll play a key role in developing strategies for the European short-term power markets.

This isn't a narrow coding or analyst role. You'll have an end-to-end mandate, from prototyping and data engineering to strategy implementation, backtesting and low-latency execution in our algorithmic trading framework. You'll own your projects from idea to P&L, working autonomously alongside a close-knit group of software engineers, quantitative researchers and expert traders.

So, if you feel energized by the intersection of markets, advanced analytics and trading technology and you want to help build something that moves power to where it’s needed the most, then we must talk.

Responsibilities

• Research and model the markets: Analyse energy market dynamics and turn your insights into predictive models that drive profitable trading strategies.

• Own the data: Build and maintain high-quality datasets that combine fundamental and real-time market data.

• Take strategies to production and keep them running: Own the path from research to live trading, shaping the systems, forecasting tools and data pipelines that run our strategies in real time. Once they're live, you'll monitor their performance, handle issues as they come up and make sure they trade reliably day to day.

• Shape the team's direction: Work closely with engineers, quantitative researchers and traders to challenge ideas, share expertise and influence where we take our algorithmic trading next.

• Master the domain: Become a domain expert and understand algorithmic trading architectures and order execution logic in the short-term power markets.

Who are you?

You have:

• Software and data skills: Advanced Python skills, and the ability to write clean, efficient, reliable code, backed by solid computer science fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, system design). Strong data skills, from sourcing and cleaning to structuring complex datasets. Some experience with C++ would be a plus.

• Ownership: The ability to work independently and deliver in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong communication: Excellent problem-solving and communication skills with full professional proficiency in English.

• Domain knowledge: A genuine interest in learning about power markets and systems. If you already have that domain knowledge, then that is a big plus.

• Education: An advanced degree in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science or Engineering.

What We Offer

• Growth environment: Be part of a young, ambitious, and expanding tech-driven trading company where talented people are given responsibility and room to grow.

• Exceptional team: Work closely with experienced quantitative researchers, software engineers and power traders.

• Competitive compensation and flexibility: Receive a competitive salary package with benefits and enjoy flexible work arrangements that support your work-life balance.

• Strong culture: Participate in both social and professional events, including team sports, company parties, teambuilding and informal gatherings that strengthen our team spirit.

• Central Copenhagen location: Work from our office in Carlsberg Byen, located in beautifully renovated historic Carlsberg buildings.

About Copenhagen Energy Trading

Copenhagen Energy Trading A/S was founded in 2021 and is part of Copenhagen Energy Group.

We specialize in short-term power trading across Europe and North America. Through technology, data, and market expertise, we develop discretionary and algorithmic trading strategies that help move power to where it is needed most.

Based in Copenhagen, we are building a collaborative, high-performance environment where talented people are trusted with responsibility and given the freedom to make an impact.

The National Museum’s Conservation and Restoration unit is seeking a conservator for a 2-year project, focusing on recent wood conservation within the museum, with a focus on church furnishings and furniture.

Work areas

You will be part of a team of conservators with many specialties. Your main responsibility will be the conservation and documentation of wooden objects, furniture, and interiors, as well as the dismantling and assembly of interiors in historic buildings and churches. The tasks also include preventive conservation. The work is part of the unit’s revenue-generating business.

In addition, there may be tasks within the National Museum’s own exhibitions, involving work with installations, exhibition care, and possibly in our magazines.

Qualifications

We expect you to have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in conservation from a recognized educational institution or equivalent. In addition, we will emphasize that you have the following:

• Practical experience with the conservation of wooden objects or knowledge of traditional craft techniques within carpentry or furniture making

• Experience with the conservation of cultural and historical objects that are still in use. Specific experience with church furnishings is desirable, but not a requirement

• Experience with pest control, treatment of fungally infected wood and stabilization of decayed wood, including the conservation of wooden objects exhibited outdoors

• Experience with budgeting and time management

• Good teamwork skills

• Driving license (B)

Wage and employment conditions

The average working hours are 37 hours per week. We have flexible hours. Wage and employment conditions are determined according to the current collective agreement for academics in the State or the organizational agreement for technical employees.

The workplace is Brede north of Copenhagen. There will be business trips of shorter or longer periods in relation to specific projects.

The National Museum must have the opportunity to assess a criminal record for private use prior to employment.

The position is to be filled with effect from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is limited in time to 2 years.

Application

The National Museum’s ambition is to create a workplace where diversity is not only tolerated, but actively promoted and valued. We therefore encourage all qualified individuals, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

We are actively working to reduce bias in the recruitment process to ensure a diverse workforce and to ensure that we hire the most suitable candidates based on professional and personal qualifications. We therefore ask that you refrain from adding a photo to your CV.

Written applications (in Danish or English) with information about education and previous employment should be sent via our electronic recruitment system on the National Museum’s website and must reach the museum no later than Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

We expect to hold job interviews at the beginning of week 49.
